merger_name: Coles – supermarket site in Narangba East, Qld
merger_description:
Coles Group Limited (**Coles**) is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that primarily operates:

* supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd; and
* retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland, Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.

Coles also has a property development arm, Coles Group Property Developments Ltd, that buys land and constructs shopping centres, standalone supermarkets and / or liquor outlets and then sells these completed sites to third party buyers.

The vendor, Consolidated Properties Group Pty Ltd, is an Australian development company with experience developing residential, commercial and retail projects. A wholly owned subsidiary of Consolidated Properties Group Pty Ltd, OptionCo Pty Ltd (the **Lessor**), is the proposed lessor in respect of the Narangba East Site (defined below).

Coles entered into a letter of offer with the Lessor in late 2024 in respect of a proposed leasehold interest for a supermarket at a new neighbourhood centre in Narangba East (the **Narangba East Site**). The Narangba East Site is located in the eastern part of Narangba, a suburb approximately 38 km north of the Brisbane CBD within the City of Moreton Bay.

Following revisions to the site layout arising from the initial development approval process, the parties now propose to enter into an Agreement for Lease. The revised layout relocates the proposed supermarket within the same neighbourhood centre and involves a minor reduction in gross lettable area (the **Acquisition**).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition may raise competition issues given:
a. Coles’ share in the supply of grocery products within a
3km radius of the Narangba East Site is expected to be
substantial if the proposed supermarket opens
b. if the Coles supermarket under construction in Narangba
also opens, Coles would operate two supermarkets
within a 5 km radius of each other, increasing Coles'
presence in the local area
c. the extent to which Coles is likely to be constrained by
alternative grocery retailers in and around the
surrounding local area is uncertain
d. the Acquisition may result in a loss of future competition
because Coles’ expansion in the Narangba East local
and surrounding area may disincentivise alternative
grocery retailers from entering the local area.
The ACCC considers that these potential competition issues warrant
consideration through the notification process, including via
consultation with third parties.
The ACCC does not consider it necessary to reach a concluded view
on the likelihood of the notification thresholds determined under
section 51ABP(1) being met. The ACCC observes there are separate
notification requirements for supermarkets determined under
section 51ABQ(1) but also does not consider it necessary to reach a
concluded view on whether they apply.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
